incidents.summary: Morgan Sindall Property Services faces nine fire-safety charges concerning its role at the Beechmere retirement village, which burnt down in August 2019.

sources.title: Firms charged over retirement village blaze | Construction News
sources.quote: Six companies, including Morgan Sindall Property Services, have been charged with breaches of fire safety laws over their role in the construction of a retirement village which burnt down in August 2019.

sources.title: Firms charged over retirement village blaze | Construction News
sources.quote: Now Morgan Sindall Property Services, which served as the facilities management subcontractor at the building and had contracted MAC Roofing and Contractors for roofing work, is facing nine charges.

sources.title: Firms charged over retirement village blaze | Construction News
sources.quote: The fire service alleges Morgan Sindall Property Services failed “to take measures to prevent the spread of fire in the premises” and failed to review a 2009 fire risk assessment which identified defective doors to the smoke shaft.

positives: Morgan Sindall Construction received BS 99001 quality-management certification under a scheme supporting Building Safety Act implementation and regulatory compliance.

incidents.summary: Basildon Borough Council is set to terminate Morgan Sindall’s £300m housing-maintenance contract, saying its work has not been good enough.

sources.title: Morgan Sindall News, Contracts and Projects | Construction News
sources.quote: Basildon Council to end Morgan Sindall’s £300m housing contract

sources.title: Morgan Sindall News, Contracts and Projects | Construction News
sources.quote: Basildon Borough Council is set to end its relationship with Morgan Sindall as the contractor’s housing maintenance work “has not been good enough”.

sources.title: Morgan Sindall News, Contracts and Projects | Construction News
sources.quote: The Essex authority threatened to terminate Morgan Sindall’s lucrative contract in February, with council leader Gavin Callaghan criticising the “diabolical state” of housing repairs.
